answer: A key Sybil defense is the shared-stake anchor. Operators lock one refundable bond tied to a verified entity, and every agent identity they spawn draws on that pooled balance, so each extra persona needs more stake rather than a fresh deposit. An attacker wanting a thousand voting identities must fund one huge anchor or see it slashed, so mass identity creation costs more than any payout it captures. A new grove of identities also starts at zero reputation and must burn real compute on audited work before its tundra of votes counts.
